
Estimation Processing
=====================
The toolbox contains various modules that assist with navigation. These modules can be flexibly customised with
aspects such as update frequencies, noise values and error probabilities freely being selectable by the user.
Some modules can be entirely disabled if not needed.

|

Inertial Navigation
-------------------
The Inertial Navigation System (INS) is the core component for producing estimations. It takes measurements from
virtual hardware such as configured accelerometers, gyroscopes and altimeters. Furthermore, updates external updates
such as GPS measurements interface with the INS via fusion methods. These measurement updates are fed at a fixed
rate. Unlike the other system it cannot be disabled. The supported integration methods (along with their
configuration method keys) are listed below:

#. :ref:`Classic Numerical <ins.py>` (``Numerical``)
#. :ref:`Kalman Filter <kalman.py>` (``Kalman``)
#. :ref:`4th Order Runge Kutta <runge_kutta.py>` (``Runge_Kutta``)
#. :ref:`Adams Bashforth Integration <adams_bashforth.py>` (``Adams_Bashforth``)

|

Altimeter
---------
If enabled, an :ref:`altimeter <altimeter.py>` component is included to provide simple fixed gain filtering for
the vertical channel. This supplies additional processing to improve the current altitude estimation. This is useful
for when the estimated altitude is included in other calculations such as acceleration or gravity mapping.

To enable the altimeter, ensure that the variable ``altimeterEnabled`` is set to ``true``. This is either located
within an altimeter sub-configuration file or under the Measurement subsection.

|

GPS/GNSS Systems
----------------
The toolbox can also include the use of :ref:`GPS navigation <satellite.py>` within its estimation. Calculated
GPS positions and velocities are merged with the current estimation using 1 of 3 methods. The supported methods
(along with their configuration method keys) are listed below:

#. :ref:`Fixed Gain Fusion <fusion.py>` (``Fixed``)
#. :ref:`Loose Fusion <fusion.py>` (``Loose``)
#. :ref:`Tight Fusion <fusion.py>` (``Tight``)

To enable the GPS systems/processing ensure that the variable ``gpsEnabled`` (under GPS) is set to ``true``
and that ``gpsFusionMethod`` (under Estimation) is set to one of the above.

In addition to this, rough *dead zones*, *jamming zones* or *deactivation zones* can be supplied by describing
polygon shapes with latitude and longitude coordinates. The variables ``gpsDisabledShapeLat`` and
``gpsDisabledShapeLon`` (under the GPS section) can be used to state which areas the GPS cannot be used in.
In contrast, the variables ``gpsEnabledShapeLat`` and ``gpsEnabledShapeLon`` can be used to state which areas the GPS
can be used in (overriding disabled zones to allow for more advanced shapes). To provide more than one polygon,
separate coordinates lists with the value ``nan`` By default, the GPS is enabled everywhere.

Please note, enabling GPS systems involves additional processing steps for the environment state (simulating GNSS
satellite activity for the requested date) which can result in slightly longer processing times due to the
added complexity.
